Sensitivity Analysis for Sample Size Planning From the AIPE Perspective for a Semipartial Correlation

Source: R/ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity.Rd

Quantifies how much misspecification of the population semipartial correlation, or of the full-model squared multiple correlation, distorts an AIPE-based sample size plan. The function constructs a \((p + 1) \times (p + 1)\) population covariance matrix for Y, X, and \(Z_1, \ldots, Z_{p-1}\) whose semipartial correlation between Y and X (partialing \(Z_1, \ldots, Z_{p-1}\) out of X only, not out of Y) equals true_r_sp and whose full-model \(R^2\) equals true_R2_full. On each replication it draws an N-row sample, computes the sample semipartial correlation and the sample full-model \(R^2\), and forms the Wald interval that ss_aipe_semipartial_r plans for: the estimate plus and minus the normal critical value times the square root of the first-order variance (var_semipartial_r with under_null = FALSE) at the two sample values.

Usage

ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity(
  true_r_sp = NULL,
  supposed_r_sp = NULL,
  p,
  width,
  specified_N = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  G = 1000,
  print_iter = FALSE,
  filename = NULL,
  true_R2_full = NULL,
  supposed_R2_full = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_r_sp

Population semipartial correlation \(\rho_{sp}\); must lie in \((-1, 1)\).

supposed_r_sp

Planning value passed to ss_aipe_semipartial_r; supply this or specified_N but not both.

p

Number of predictors in the regression of Y on X and the variables partialed out, so p - 1 variables are partialed out and p is at least 2. A categorical variable with a levels counts as a - 1 predictors. It is the p of ss_power_R2, ci_R2, and ci_reg_coef: the correlation concerns one predictor of a regression with p predictors. In the notation of a model comparison, \(q\) is the number of predictors removed from the full model to give the restricted model (\(q = p_{full} - p_{restricted}\), the predictors being tested), and the number of variables partialed out is \(p - q\); this correlation concerns one predictor, so \(q = 1\) and \(p - 1\) variables are partialed out. The simulated data have \(p + 1\) columns.

width

Desired full width of the CI on the semipartial correlation.

specified_N

Sample size to evaluate; a whole number of at least \(p + 2\).

conf_level

Confidence level (default 0.95).

assurance

Optional assurance probability passed to ss_aipe_semipartial_r; used only with supposed_r_sp.

G

Number of Monte Carlo replications (default 1000).

print_iter

Logical. Print the iteration index of each replication.

filename

Optional path for a comma separated file recording every replication (the sample semipartial correlation, the two confidence limits, the interval width, and two indicators of whether the interval missed true_r_sp below or above): nothing is written when filename is NULL (the default), a new file with a header row is created otherwise, an existing file at that path is appended to, and a throwaway run should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv").

true_R2_full

Population squared multiple correlation of the full model (Y on X and \(Z_1, \ldots, Z_{p-1}\)); at least true_r_sp squared and below 1. When NULL (the default) it is true_r_sp squared, a population in which the variables partialed out explain none of the outcome.

supposed_R2_full

Optional planning value of the full-model \(R^2\), passed to ss_aipe_semipartial_r as true_R2_full; when NULL that function plans for the largest variance over every possible value. It cannot be given with specified_N.

seed

NULL (the default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a single number that makes the run reproducible; a supplied seed is set for this call only, and the caller's random number state is restored when the function returns. With assurance, the seed also makes the simulated plan of ss_aipe_semipartial_r reproducible.

Value

A data.frame with rows for the realized semipartial correlation, the interval width, the proportion of intervals at or below width, tail-specific and overall non-coverage of true_r_sp, and the input echoes, including true_R2_full (the value simulated), supposed_R2_full (NA when none was supplied), and assurance (present only when an assurance was supplied).

Details

Under multivariate normality the sampling distribution of the sample semipartial correlation depends on the population only through the semipartial correlation, the full-model \(R^2\), \(p\), and the sample size, because the statistic is unchanged by any nonsingular linear transformation of \(Z_1, \ldots, Z_{p-1}\), by adding any linear function of them to X, and by positive rescaling of X and Y. The population simulated here (uncorrelated standardized X and \(Z_1, \ldots, Z_{p-1}\), with Y related to X and to \(Z_1\)) therefore stands for every normal population with the same two values.

The confidence limits are not truncated at \(-1\) and \(1\), so that the widths are those the planner plans; with a large \(|\rho_{sp}|\) and a small sample a limit can pass 1 in absolute value.

The function simulates \(p - 1\) variables partialed out, the count ss_aipe_semipartial_r plans for.

With assurance, the sample size comes from the simulated assurance step of ss_aipe_semipartial_r (at its default number of draws), so two unseeded calls can simulate sample sizes that differ by a case or two.

A value of true_R2_full or supposed_R2_full that falls below the squared semipartial correlation by no more than rounding to two decimals allows is taken to mean that the variables partialed out explain none of the outcome, with a warning of class dmar_semipartial_r_rounded; a smaller value is refused.

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Kelley, K., & Maxwell, S. E. (2003). Sample size for multiple regression: Obtaining regression coefficients that are accurate, not simply significant. Psychological Methods, 8(3), 305–321. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.8.3.305

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge.

Examples

# G = 50 keeps the example quick; a reported check deserves the
# default G = 1000 or more.
ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity(
  true_r_sp = 0.30, supposed_r_sp = 0.30, p = 4, width = 0.20,
  G = 50, print_iter = FALSE,
  true_R2_full = 0.50, supposed_R2_full = 0.50, seed = 113
)
